stemMd: Which formula represents a saturated acyclic hydrocarbon with five carbon atoms?
explanationMd: An acyclic saturated hydrocarbon is an alkane with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. For n = 5, hydrogen count is 12. The word acyclic excludes cycloalkanes, which have two fewer hydrogens for one ring.

distractorRationale.e: This has two fewer hydrogens, consistent with one ring or one double bond.
distractorRationale.b: This has further unsaturation compared with an acyclic alkane.
distractorRationale.d: This is far short of the hydrogen count for an acyclic saturated hydrocarbon.
distractorRationale.c: This exceeds the normal hydrogen count allowed for an acyclic five-carbon alkane.
